title: I built vimeo-cli, a command line tool for Vimeo
partialText: vimeo-cli is my free, open source command line tool for Vimeo. One command uploads a video, applies the player preset I use on every video, and prints the link to share.

title: I built Blips, 6,000 8-bit sound effects for my apps
partialText: Blips is my free, open source Mac app and command line tool with about 6,000 8-bit sound effects made with jsfxr. Click a sound to hear it, drag it into your app.

title: I built Snake, the classic phone game for the Apple TV
partialText: Snake is my free, open source Apple TV game: the classic snake game from old mobile phones, full screen on a green LCD board, steered by swiping on the Siri Remote.

title: How to use cf, the new Cloudflare CLI
partialText: Learn cf, the new Cloudflare CLI: find commands with cf cli search, configure Workers in cloudflare.config.ts, deploy, and migrate from Wrangler.

title: Hosting picker: find where to host your app
partialText: Answer four questions and get three hosts that fit your project, with a monthly price and the main catch. 21 providers, prices checked October 1, 2026.

title: Payment picker: find how to get paid for your app
partialText: Find a payment provider for your product, compare fees on your own numbers, and see who handles tax and disputes. Merchant of Record and direct providers.

title: A deep dive into cron
partialText: Learn cron on Linux and macOS: crontab syntax, schedules, the cron environment, logs, overlapping runs, time zones, launchd and systemd timers.

title: I built Blueprint, a Mac app that shows how my apps are built
partialText: Blueprint is my free, open source Mac app that draws how your apps are built, their workflows and the data they store, from maps your coding agents write.

title: How to sync a Mac app with its iPhone app
partialText: How to sync a Mac app and its iPhone companion: CloudKit, what the Apple Developer Program unlocks, iCloud for apps outside the App Store, and alternatives.

title: I built Notion Presenter View, a Chrome extension that shows your next slide
partialText: Notion Presenter View is my free, open source Chrome extension that shows the next slide of a Notion presentation in a small floating window, on top of the fullscreen slides.

title: How my Mac apps update themselves from GitHub Releases
partialText: Soundscape and CLI Tools check GitHub once a day, download the new release, verify it, and replace themselves. Here's how it works, in one Swift file with no dependencies.

title: How to let coding agents test Mac apps in a VM
partialText: Run a headless macOS VM with Tart so coding agents can launch, screenshot and click through your Mac apps without taking over your screen.

title: Should you pay for the Apple Developer Program?
partialText: Free Apple developer account vs the $99 Apple Developer Program: what each lets you do, what changes when you pay, and why it helps outside the App Store too.

title: How to fix "Stacked PRs are not enabled for this repository"
partialText: Stacked PRs are not enabled for this repository is a gh stack warning with no setting to flip. Check your gh account and repo, or open regular PRs.

title: How to use Jev confidence scores
partialText: How to use Jev confidence scores to decide when code acts, asks for confirmation, or hands off to a person, with thresholds tuned on labeled data.

title: I built VM Monitor, a Mac app that shows what your coding agents do in the test VM
partialText: VM Monitor is my free, open source Mac app that shows what coding agents do in a macOS test VM: its screen live, which agents are using it and for what, and every command they ran.

title: I built Postdeck, slides from posts on X for my videos
partialText: Postdeck is my free, open source Mac app and Chrome extension that turn posts on X into slides. Click the slide icon under a post, reorder the slides, and play them in the app window while you record.

title: How to classify text with Jev
partialText: How to classify text with Jev: pick Noul, Choice or Score, write labels that work, label comments in bulk, and test accuracy before you trust it.

title: What is poteto-mode in pstack?
partialText: poteto-mode is the pstack router skill for Cursor. Describe a result and it picks a playbook, calls the other skills, delegates to models and verifies the work.

title: How to create and publish a ChatGPT plugin
partialText: Create a ChatGPT plugin from scratch: a booking MCP server, a skill and a plugin.json package, tested in developer mode and submitted to the directory.

title: Herdr alternatives for running coding agents
partialText: Herdr alternatives compared: cmux, tmux, Zellij, workmux, worktrunk, T3 Code and bb, with platforms, agent status, worktrees and what to use on Linux.

title: What running a one-person software business costs per month
partialText: What my one-person software business costs each month, line by line: hosting, email, analytics, payment fees, domains, software and AI tools.

title: I built Factory Log, a Mac app that shows what your coding agents did
partialText: Factory Log is my free, open source Mac app that turns the one-line reports your coding agents write into a timeline of your day and week, and shows where your time went, project by project.

title: How to use your ChatGPT subscription in other apps
partialText: Sign in with ChatGPT lets Plus and Pro users spend their plan in Devin, Warp, Notion, Pi and other apps. How to connect one, cap it, and build your own.

title: How to use the Codex CLI
partialText: How to use the Codex CLI, OpenAI's coding agent for the terminal: install it, run tasks, set permissions, pick a model, review changes and use codex exec.

title: I built Calculum for Mac, 281 calculators that work offline
partialText: Calculum for Mac is my free, open source app with the 281 calculators from calculum.dev. It works offline, saves and compares calculations, and comes with a calculum command for Terminal.

title: Every product I launched this summer, and what happened to each
partialText: Every product I launched between July and September 2026, in date order: what each one is, why I built it, and what happened to it since.

title: A deep dive into Clef, Cloudflare's decision model
partialText: Clef is Cloudflare's open-weight decision model on Workers AI. How it works, how to call it, and how it compares with Jev and OpenAI's Decisions API.

title: I built Releases, a Mac app that tracks every app I release
partialText: Releases is my free, open source Mac app that shows every release of my apps on one timeline, tells me what's waiting to ship, and starts the next release in Cursor.

title: I built Tab Merger, a Chrome extension that merges all your windows into one
partialText: Tab Merger is my free, open source Chrome extension that moves the tabs of every open window into the one you're using, with one click or a keyboard shortcut.
